messages:
alex: Heads-up — brought up q4 reranker (cross-encoder) on webqa holdout and seeing ~3.1% relative drop in NDCG@10 vs fp16. MRR stable.
mira: can you paste the exact eval command and split you used? sample size? :thinking:
alex: eval command:
```
python eval.py --model reranker-cross-q4_0 --dataset webqa_holdout --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --samples 10k
```
split = webqa_holdout_v2 (10k queries sampled stratified by frequency)
jonathan: curious — NDCG drops but MRR stable suggests tail relevance shifts. do we have per-rank breakdowns? ndcg@1,3,10?
alex: output snippet:
```
ndcg@1: 0.421 -> 0.419 (-0.5%)
ndcg@3: 0.612 -> 0.594 (-2.9%)
ndcg@10: 0.741 -> 0.718 (-3.1%)
mrr: 0.536 -> 0.534 (-0.4%)
```
eva: that pattern smells like slight score smoothing/scale change after quant. q4 tends to compress logits a bit, ordering for mid-ranked docs can flip.
mira: do we normalize scores before ranking? training used softmax cross-entropy; eval pipeline applies raw logits for sorting.
jonathan: if scale changes, softmax-based calibration or monotonic transform might help. Also check doc length truncation — quantization can change tokenization rounding in our packaging? improbable but seen before.
alex: double-checked tokenization — same tokenizer, same max_seq_len=512. but reranker input formatting changed: we moved from "title \n body" to "title - body" in a recent PR. could affect where relevant spans sit relative to truncation.
eva: good catch — format change could shift relevance if title held the cue. Can we compare title+body vs body-only slices?
sam: we should also run bootstrap significance for the observed drop. 3% relative at ndcg@10 might be noise depending on sample. I'll run 1000 bootstrap resamples.
alex: ran quick paired bootstrap (n=1000) — p-value ~0.02 for ndcg@10, 95% CI for delta = [-0.052, -0.011] (relative). so looks significant.
mira: ok so not pure noise. propose ablation matrix:
- quant config: q4_0 vs q4_1 vs fp16
- input format: title+body vs body-only vs title-first
- dataset slices: head(>100q), mid, tail(<5q)
- scoring: raw logits vs sigmoid-calibrated vs isotonic
please prioritize quant configs and input format first.
jonathan: add model-level logging: store top-5 candidate deltas per query so we can inspect where flips happen. also tag cases where doc lengths > 400 tokens.
eva: also try per-slice calibration (learn a linear scale+shift on a small val set) — often fixes monotonic distortions from quant.
alex: i'll run the ablations. initial estimate: 48 runs but can parallelize. timeline 48h.
sam: bootstrap job queued — will post summary when done (cc @eval-bot)
eva: if input-format ablation explains most of drop then revert formatting PR and add unit test to prevent silent formatting drift.
mira: action items:
- alex: run ablation matrix, collect top-5 diffs, assign hypothesis tags (format vs quant) — due in 48h
- sam: run bootstrap + per-slice significance, attach p-values and CIs — due 24h
- jonathan: add eval logging + query-level diff export into results schema — due 24h
- eva: try linear calibration on val split and report ndcg lift — due 24h
we good?
sam: yep. I'll post interim results here.
eval-bot: scheduled job 1786123500 started: reranker_quant_ablation (48 tasks). logs: https://ci.internal/runs/1786123500
alex: thanks everyone. if format is root cause we should patch ASAP (small rollback). otherwise we may need to revisit quant config (q4_1) or per-customer fallback to fp16 for critical slices.
mira: thanks — keep notes short in PRs so DS can audit decisions. :thumbsup:
